original_record.canonical_name: The International Award for Young People (Duke of Edinburgh's International Award)
original_record.organizer: The International Award Foundation (global); operated in Türkiye by TİKAV (Türkiye İnsan Kaynağını Geliştirme Vakfı)
original_record.eligibility_verbatim: available to all 14 to 24-year-olds, inclusive of all backgrounds, locations, cultures and abilities (global site); Turkey operator: '14 - 24 yaş aralığında olmanız yeterlidir'. Level-specific minimum ages in Turkey: Bronze 14+, Silver 15+, Gold 16+.

original_record.turkey_access_reasoning: TİKAV (Türkiye İnsan Kaynağını Geliştirme Vakfı) is the officially licensed national operator for Türkiye, confirmed on both intaward.org (global) and intaward.org.tr (Turkey). Open to any student aged 14-24 via a participating school's Award Coordinator, or by independent/individual application by emailing bagimsiz@tikav.org.tr with no school-nomination gatekeeping required. No citizenship restriction found; open to Turkey residents generally.
original_record.international_access_notes: Operates in 120+ countries; the Bronze/Silver/Gold certificate is portable and internationally recognized, useful on applications to universities outside Türkiye as well as within it.
original_record.minimum_activity_duration: Bronze: minimum 6 months; Silver: minimum 12 months; Gold: minimum 18 months (across Volunteering, Skills, Physical, and Expedition sections; Gold adds a 5th Community Service Project section).
original_record.geographic_restrictions: None found beyond needing a licensed national operator (Türkiye has one via TİKAV); open to all youth in Türkiye regardless of background per official copy.
original_record.current_cycle_label: Rolling enrollment; not a fixed annual application cycle
original_record.cost_notes: Turkey operator confirms an annual 'Katılım Bağışı' (participation donation) is required before starting; exact current TL amount not stated on the pages fetched directly. A secondary (non-official) source cited approx. 150 TL -- not independently confirmed by us against an official price list, so left unset rather than guessed.

reasoning: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO) — live DB already has "USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)" (usaco.org), filed under category=competition.

original_record.eligibility_verbatim: USACO 'supports computing education in the USA and worldwide by identifying, motivating, and training high-school computing students at all levels' (official About page). Online contest registration itself carries no stated nationality restriction; Training Camp invitations and USA-team selection for IOI/EGOI are explicitly for US pre-college students.
original_record.turkey_access_reasoning: Multiple independent secondary sources (Lumiere Education, AdmissionSight, enthu.com, TeenLife) consistently and specifically state that students from any country can register a free usaco.org account and compete in the online Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum contests at no cost; only Training Camp invitations and official USA-team selection for IOI/EGOI are restricted to US pre-college students. This specific international-access sentence was not itself found verbatim on an official USACO page during this pass (see notes).
original_record.international_access_notes: A Turkey-based student gets full access to the free online contest ladder and division certification, but not camp/team-selection benefits (not a meaningful loss for this use case — division placement itself is the college-application-relevant signal).
original_record.current_cycle_label: USACO runs several contests per year (December, January/February, and the US Open in Spring)
original_record.cost_notes: Free — no entry fee; only a free usaco.org account is required.
original_record.output_type_notes: Real competitive-programming problems solved under timed contest conditions; Platinum-division placement in particular is a well-recognized, meaningful signal in US college admissions for CS-interested applicants.

evidence.raw_excerpt: Supports computing education in the USA and worldwide by identifying, motivating, and training high-school computing students at all levels... free on-line training resources and historical contest problems... four competitive tiers: bronze, silver, gold, and platinum... highest-ranked individuals may represent the USA at the International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI) or European Girls' Olympiad in Informatics (EGOI).

original_record.notes_uncertainties: Core program facts confirmed on USACO's own official About page. The specific 'any country may register and compete online for free' claim is corroborated by several independent, mutually-consistent secondary sources but repeated WebFetch attempts at usaco.org's FAQ/eligibility/contests subpages failed (socket errors) during this pass, so it was not directly re-confirmed verbatim on an official page. This is a very well-documented, low-risk fact in the competitive-programming community; reviewer should do one quick confirm pass before flipping to VERIFIED.
